rs-ss-melt.back: Sun melts them out bigger and rounder over days. Measure fresh prints only.

rs-ss-melt-trap.back: It can look like an elk print. Use shape, toes and pattern, not size.

rs-ss-depth.back: Past about 30 cm; they leave slopes past about 50 cm. Moose fine to about 40 cm.

rs-ss-wet-sand.back: Wet sand holds clear shapes. Dry sand slumps into bowls; read spacing instead.

</svg>

rs-ss-sand-age.front: Why do sand prints age fast?
rs-ss-sand-age.back: The edges dry out quickly in sun and wind.

rs-ss-dust.back: Fine detail, but rare and erased by wind. A fresh dust print has a thin raised rim.

rs-ss-overlay.front: Deer print on top of a tire tread?
rs-ss-overlay.back: Made after the vehicle passed. On top came last.

rs-ss-litter.front: No prints in leaves and duff: what to read?
rs-ss-litter.back: Flipped leaves, scuffed moss, pressed duff, moved stones.

Read what moved (65%)</text>
</svg>

rs-ss-grass.front: Which way did it go through grass?
rs-ss-grass.back: Bent stems lie the way the animal moved.

rs-ss-homemade.back: Smooth a strip of dirt on a trail in the evening; check it in the morning.

rs-ss-ice.back: Not trustworthy. Do not cross to save a kilometre.

rs-ss-variability.front: Why do tracks of one animal look so different?
rs-ss-variability.back: Ground (snow, mud, dust, sand) and speed change how a track looks.
